topic.title: Dyatlov Pass, 1959: the tent cut open from the inside
topic.angle: Nine experienced hikers in the northern Urals cut their tent open from inside and fled into the snow, many without shoes; all died; Soviet file said 'a compelling natural force'; 2020 Russian review said avalanche; many still doubt
key_facts: In February 1959 nine experienced hikers led by Igor Dyatlov were on the slopes of Kholat Syakhl in the northern Ural mountains
Searchers found their tent cut open from the inside; footprints led downhill, many were without shoes in about -25 to -30 C
All nine died; bodies were found between February and May
The Soviet investigation closed the case citing 'a compelling natural force'
Theories over decades included yeti, secret weapons tests and aliens
In 2020 Russian prosecutors concluded a small slab avalanche; a 2021 study (Gaume & Puzrin) found it plausible; many still doubt it
